rv.q: Holden's performance, directed by Bronagh Lagan, is captivating - whether he's switching between accents, channelling his inner diva for a hysterical rendition of Peggy Lee's All There Is, or dancing what he believes to be his last dance, he will have you laughing and crying in equal measure.
One year on, with life returned largely to normal, that raw resonant power remains intact, the play an enduring life affirming tribute to a vanished queer history.
I honestly cannot state how much Cruise blew me away and I don’t think there are enough superlatives to express my thoughts on it.
Holden has written one of the great plays of the last year so don’t miss this second chance to go cruising.

CRUISE is based on Jack Holden’s personal experiences volunteering in his youth at the London Gay Switchboard Helpline during the 1980s — and he deploys a particularly effective device to segue the audience into that hedonistic lost realm.

It was one of the first productions to premiere in the West End when theatres first reopened in May 2021, instantly winning critical acclaim and was even nominated for Best New Play at this years Olivier awards. More than that, it was also one of my personal favourite shows of last year.

Having starred on Amazon Prime’s Ten Percent and played the lead in War Horse he just thought he would simply write his own West End debut and star in it. But luminous jealousy aside, this Olivier-nominated piece was the first new play to open on the West End during lockdown.
